newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen inactive, or adding 4-day systems Thurs..
newsitem.headline: Fed seen inactive, or adding 4-day systems Thurs..

text.p: The Federal Reserve was expected to either remain out of the banking system or execute four-day system repurchase agreements during its usual midmorning intervention period Thursday, economists said.
Carol Stone, economist at Nomura Securities International Inc., said that under the Fed's new system of reporting operations, it was fairly safe to say no action would be undertaken.
"We now know under the new methods that they have covered their needs for this half of the maintenance period. There will be some runoff on Monday, so they may have to come back in then," Stone said.
Marilyn Schaja, money market economist at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp, also saw the Fed remaining on the sideline as did analysts at MCM Moneywatch.
"They surprised me yesterday with a rather large five-day operation, so you never know," Schaja said. "But I don't expect them back into until Monday."
However, economists at UBS Securities expected to see another round of four-day system RPs as its add need remains sufficiently strong.
The federal funds rate opened at 5-13/16 percent and was last trading right at the Fed's current official target level of 5.25 percent.
-- John P. Hughes, N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1663
